mentions.name: html-traits
mentions.description: A JavaScript/HTML library that adds behaviors to existing HTML elements via a `traits` attribute instead of the web components `is` attribute. Designed for progressive enhancement: elements keep working when JavaScript is disabled or broken, and gain behaviors when JS runs—for example an `expando` trait that makes a textarea auto-expand, or a `character-limit` trait with a `data-character-limit="200"` attribute that turns the box red past a threshold. Behaviors compose as plain attributes on the element, avoiding nested web component markup and shadow-DOM reimplementation of native element behavior.
mentions.problem: Normal web components lead to nested element markup or hide the original element in the shadow DOM, forcing developers to reimplement native behavior; and elements break entirely when JavaScript fails or is disabled.
mentions.audience: Developers building web pages with HTML/JavaScript
mentions.source_excerpt: I built a simple lib for JS/HTML called html-traits[1]. It's similar to built-in web components but instead of using the `is` attribute you use the `traits` attribute. So, it is specifically meant for progressive enhancement.
